text:
Emma: FYI - Summit (POC) hit recurring slow TTFTs this morning after a burst test. Customer says it started at ~09:10 PT, now intermittently 700-1200ms first token.
Sanjay: thanks, grabbing logs and routing info. are they on dedicated or hosted?
Emma: hosted, standard plan. They tried enabling prefill per our presales guide.
Jana: do we have the prefill policy they used? prefill can conflict with batching window and cause queueing.
Emma: Olivia pushed this config: `prefill: enabled, prefill_batch_window_ms: 200, max_prefill_tokens: 512` — customer docs attached in the ticket.
Sanjay: that batch_window is pretty small; with concurrent streams it can increase enqueue jitter. can you paste a small sample of the request headers and model name?
Olivia: model is `redwood-2-8b-quant`, client concurrency ~12, mean prompt len 120 tokens.
Eli: customer says they saw 429s briefly, then TTFT spikes. no full error dumps in the UI.
Ops-bot: recent deploy tag `runtime-v2.13.1` rolled 09:03 PT to region `us-west-2`. No infra alerts.
Jana: ok two things to check: 1) KV cache warmup status (prefill writes to KV then subsequent requests read; cold misses can amplify TTFT), 2) shard queue saturation due to prefill and normal requests mixing.
Sanjay: can you run this quick diagnostic on a failing session: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/diag/session -d '{"session_id":"<id>","include":"queue,kvcache"}'` and paste output?
Emma: customer pasted this excerpt: ``logs: queue_wait_ms=312, kvcache_miss=true, backend_latency_ms=78``
Jana: that kvcache_miss=true is the smoking gun. prefill policy with small batch windows can cause a write then immediate read race across shards.
Sanjay: mitigation options: 1) temporarily disable prefill to see TTFT baseline, 2) increase prefill_batch_window_ms to 800-1000ms so prefill batches reduce KV thrash, or 3) enable `prefill_strict_sequencing: true` (serializes prefill writes per session) — option 3 increases latency for prefill but stabilizes reads.
Olivia: customer worried about SLA impact — they asked if we can offer credits for the POC day(s) with instability.
Eli: we can propose a goodwill credit equal to one day's hosted usage if disabling prefill and config change don't resolve within 24h. need approval from sales ops.
Sanjay: short-term patch I'd recommend: disable prefill, rerun the burst, confirm TTFT drops. If that works, we can do controlled re-enable with `prefill_batch_window_ms: 1000` and monitor.
Emma: customer ready for a 30-min call. can we join now?
Jana: available. will bring a small script to tail per-shard queue lengths.
Sanjay: I'll bring the KV metrics and a runbook.
Olivia: I'll handle the credits ask and loop in finance if needed.
Eli: customer follow-up note: "We rely on first-token p50 < 300ms for interactive demo."
Sanjay: noted. if disabling prefill gets p50 < 300ms we confirm prefill as root cause. also watch for burst-related throttles — check `x-ratelimit-remaining` in responses.
Emma: customer ran quick disable test — reported p50 ~ 220ms, no 429s during a 5-min window.
Olivia: great, let's propose the config change and schedule a controlled re-enable next morning with us observing. I'll draft email with next steps and the credit pledge conditional on no resolution after config change.
Jana: technical follow-up to paste in email: include this snippet to change config via API: 
```
PATCH /v1/projects/<proj>/settings
Content-Type: application/json
{ "prefill": { "enabled": true, "prefill_batch_window_ms": 1000, "prefill_strict_sequencing": false } }
```
Sanjay: also include command to fetch session diag: `curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/diag/session/<id>?fields=queue,kvcache`
Ops-bot: note added to ticket #4591: "Performed temporary prefill disable; p50 improved to 220ms. Pending config re-enable with larger batch window and monitor."
Emma: customer happy to proceed. scheduling re-enable TOM 09:00 PT with on-call watch. thanks team :thumbsup:
Olivia: I'll update the deal notes with the temporary credit offer and timeline.
Eli: closing loop with customer now. will post call summary once done.
Sanjay: follow-up action items: ["monitor kvcache hit-rate during re-enable","capture per-shard queue metrics","verify no 429s after ramp"]
Emma: copying the plan into the POC ticket. thanks everyone.
